answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can weight each identity by its verifiable work history, like a voyage log that cannot be faked overnight. Every completed job is countersigned by the counterparty and chained to the agent's record, so trust accrues slowly and only through real effort. A sock-puppet starts at zero, like a jade carving cut facet by facet — a prism only shines after the work is done. An attacker who fakes a thousand identities gains no reputation, and building history for each one costs the full price of real work, making the attack uneconomical.
